angle: How much of The Night Watch we see today is the painting Rembrandt actually made?
logline: It isn't a night scene, but darkened varnish gave it its name, so we ask what else isn't Rembrandt's, and the answer starts with a daylight militia march, but in 1715 it was trimmed to fit the town hall, so two men vanished, but a small copy kept them, so in 2021 AI printed the edges back, but it had nearly been lost entirely in a wartime cave.
hooks: In 1715, Amsterdam cut this painting down to fit a room.
To see this painting whole, you have to go to London.

script.text: The Night Watch isn't set at night.
Its daylight sank under darkened varnish, and the nickname stuck.
So how much of what we see is really Rembrandt's painting?
He painted a militia company marching out, in 1642.
script.say: He painted a militia company marching out, in sixteen forty-two.

script.text: Captain Banninck Cocq gives the order, his hand's shadow falling on his lieutenant's coat.
script.say: Captain Banning Cock gives the order, his hand's shadow falling on his lieutenant's coat.

script.text: So a group portrait that should stand in rows suddenly moves.
But in 1715, it moved to Amsterdam's town hall, and didn't fit.
script.say: But in seventeen fifteen, it moved to Amsterdam's town hall, and didn't fit.

script.text: So they trimmed strips off all four sides, most from the left.
Two men on the left edge vanished.
But Gerrit Lundens had painted a small copy before the cut.
So in 2021, the Rijksmuseum trained an AI on it and printed the lost edges back.
script.say: So in twenty twenty-one, the Rijksmuseum trained an A.I. on it and printed the lost edges back.

script.text: For the first time in three hundred years, it hung complete.
But in the war, it was rolled up and hidden in a cave.
So it isn't night, isn't its name, and isn't its full size.
But in a small copy in London, Rembrandt's whole company still marches out.
